title: How Cloudflare enforces engineering standards using AI
excerpt: We created the Cloudflare Codex, a governed body of engineering standards that AI agents consume across the development lifecycle. By pairing structured RFCs with agentic reviews, teams automatically enforce consistency across code, specs, and incident reports.
content_html:
Over the past four months, our AI code reviewer has flagged nearly a quarter of a million deviations from Cloudflare engineering standards (what we’ll call “violations” in this post) and blocked 16,000 merges. Our spec reviewer agent has evaluated close to 600 technical designs against the same standards before implementation began. Both systems draw from the Cloudflare Codex, a shared source of engineering guidance built for people and agents. This post explains why we built the Codex, how it supports the engineering lifecycle, and what we plan to do next.

Before the Codex (which we briefly introduced in a previous post about our AI engineering stack), developer guidance at Cloudflare lived in many places: formal documentation, repository files, chat threads, and the accumulated knowledge of individual engineers. Engineers often spent too much time searching for guidance instead of working on the problem they were trying to solve. Even after finding an answer, they could not always tell whether it was current, authoritative, or applicable to their situation.

As Cloudflare grew, that model became increasingly difficult to sustain. No engineer could read every standard, and reviewers could not reliably check every requirement. Institutional knowledge became harder to recover when people moved between teams, and guidance that was not consistently surfaced or enforced led to drift between projects.

We rebuilt this body of knowledge as the Cloudflare Codex: a governed set of engineering standards that agents can retrieve and apply at the point of work. The same guidance can now inform code review, technical design review, incident report review, and many other use cases, while engineers focus their time and judgment on the resulting findings.

Codex organization and workflow

A dedicated Codex governance model divides the Codex into distinct domains covering the engineering areas we care about. These include architectural matters (for example, frontend and control plane), cross-cutting concerns (security and reliability), specific languages (TypeScript and Rust), and several other areas. Each domain is led by an owner who is responsible for the content, consistency, and overall quality of the documents they oversee.

Codex standards use a Request for Comments (RFC) format. Requirements use the SHOULD and MUST keywords defined by RFC 2119. We also expect a front matter header to hold metadata such as the domain and RFC status. Any Cloudflare employee with a key interest and domain competency can propose an RFC through a merge request that follows the prescribed structure. The proposal then passes through several rounds of feedback from an increasingly broad group of reviewers. Once the domain owner gives final approval, the RFC becomes part of the Codex and is published to an Astro-powered internal site.

Approved RFCs can be consumed by Codex clients and agents, which may then start to flag Codex violations in code, configuration, or documentation immediately. However, they block based on Codex statements only after an RFC moves from the approved to the enforced lifecycle state. This separate promotion step gives teams time to absorb new requirements and accommodates cases where enforcement needs additional work.

The following diagram illustrates the steps in the Codex workflow:

A naive process could stop here and feed the entire Codex to a large language model (LLM) as is. Given the increasing number of RFCs we have already (60+ and counting), however, the corpus volume would put a lot of stress on the context window and impact LLM results negatively. To help guide models to the most relevant RFCs, we invoke a purpose-built agent to automatically extract and compact the SHOULD and MUST statements into a dedicated JSON structure and enrich it with metadata that supports lazy discovery and progressive disclosure. The following abridged excerpt shows the result for our control plane services RFC:

{
  "rfc": 14,
  "title": "Control Plane Services",
  "status": "approved",
  "domain": "control-plane",
  "statements": [
    {
      "slug": "use-quicksilver-for-edge-configuration-propagation",
      "section": ["Proposal", "Infrastructure"],
      "level": "SHOULD",
      "text": "If you need to propagate system or customer configuration to the edge, use Quicksilver via the outbox pattern",
      "href": "/rfcs/014-control-plane-services/#infrastructure"
    },
    {
      "slug": "api-schemas-must-be-documented-in-openapi-spec",
      "section": ["Proposal", "API Gateway"],
      "level": "MUST",
      "text": "API request and response schemas MUST be documented using an OpenAPI spec",
      "href": "/rfcs/014-control-plane-services/#api-gateway"
    }
  ]
}

Each statement receives a stable slug identifier that remains unchanged during the extraction process even when its RFC is updated. The identifier lets us track the same statement across different systems over time, which is essential for monitoring, analysis, and exception handling.

Initially, we extracted the statements into another, more concise Markdown file rather than JSON. Over time, we moved to a richer structured format so that agents could filter the content they needed more accurately. We plan to include additional metadata for even tighter scoping, such as indicators for the software development life cycle (SDLC) stage a statement applies to (e.g., design, implementation, runtime).

Codex consumers

Several systems already use the Codex in day-to-day engineering work. Three agents show how the Codex works in practice: our AI code reviewer, spec reviewer, and incident report reviewer.

AI code reviewer

Our AI code reviewer agent, covered in a separate blog post, evaluates merge requests across several dimensions, including Codex compliance.

For each review, the agent retrieves the RFCs and parses the Codex statements. It loads full RFC bodies only when the model or coordinator needs additional context. In most cases, the statements provide enough information to explain a reported violation.

The distinction between SHOULD and MUST, together with an RFC’s status, determines how the reviewer responds. Findings from approved RFCs are non-blocking recommendations. Once an RFC is enforced, an unsatisfied MUST requirement causes the reviewer to withhold approval or block a merge request, depending on the severity. 

Since the Codex’s inception earlier this year, the AI code reviewer has flagged close to 230,000 violations. Among these, almost 16,000 caused approval to be withheld (i.e., they referred to MUST statements on enforced RFCs).

Code review alternatives

A single AI code reviewer run usually takes a couple of minutes to complete due to the coordinator framework and sub-agent execution. Although the wait is very often worth the money (or tokens), engineers were calling out the delay and extra round trip involved in remediating the findings. We looked into how we could improve the experience and came up with two additional options:

  1. For language-specific Codex requirements that can be verified mechanically, we provide custom linter configuration packages. These are aligned with our Codex specification and make it possible to surface problems in milliseconds. TypeScript was the first language to receive Codex linter support while also standardizing on oxlint (maintained by the VoidZero team who joined Cloudflare recently) for performant linter execution. A linter for Rust projects is currently under development, and Go will eventually follow to complete coverage of Cloudflare’s most commonly used languages.
  2. To cut out the continuous integration (CI) leg from the review cycle, we made it possible to run the AI code reviewer locally through a command-line interface (CLI). It matches the coordinator functionality from CI and runs the same (OpenCode-based) agents against an automatically determined diff set, with results presented in the terminal.

We believe the linters would be useful to almost every developer and codebase, while the CLI remains an optional alternative for engineers who prefer it.

Spec reviewer

Engineers at Cloudflare regularly write design documents and technical specifications (or specs in short) before implementation. A significant subset of the Codex pertains to design, architecture, and other themes relevant to technical reviews. To catch architectural mistakes before implementation begins, we built the spec reviewer, an agent that discovers specs and evaluates them against relevant Codex requirements.

The spec reviewer operates on the Developer Platform: it runs as a Cloudflare Worker, stores its results and state in D1, routes model requests through AI Gateway, and kicks off scanning for new specs via a Cron Trigger. It starts by filtering the Codex by domains and sections relevant to specs (for example, language features and implementation-focused RFCs are disregarded). Several guiding prompts instruct the model on how to run the assessment and frame the results. The findings get rated based on severity (influenced by SHOULD and MUST keywords) and include general quality and architectural advice. On completion of a review run, a note is left on the spec document linking to a custom dashboard where review details can be inspected.

Since the beginning of May 2026, almost 600 unique open specs have been reviewed. Including reruns triggered on demand or by spec changes, we tracked over 3,200 review invocations to this date. The vast majority of findings had a “major” (65%) or “minor” (29%) severity, with “critical” findings being the minority (6%).

The following image gives an impression of what the spec reviewer UI looks like:

We plan to integrate the spec reviewer more tightly by posting comments directly on the spec documents, embedding human-agent conversations that can influence the review assessment, and flagging high-impact proposals for additional human review.

Incident report reviewer

The incident report reviewer applies the same approach to incident reports (also known as postmortems). In addition to checking that each report is complete, it evaluates whether the report clearly explains what happened, identifies contributing factors, documents the resolution, and proposes meaningful follow-up actions. These expectations are defined in a dedicated Codex RFC.

The incident report reviewer uses the same Developer Platform building blocks as the spec reviewer. This shared architecture is becoming a common pattern for our Codex agents.

Since May 2026, the reviewer has assessed more than 200 incident reports and identified gaps such as missing follow-up action items, incomplete timelines, and omitted detection signals. Among those reports, 93% covered incidents that were low-impact, internal-only, or declared preemptively. For high-severity incidents, we’ve made the reviewer mandatory as part of our comprehensive central review process, and reports are not considered complete until all findings have been addressed.

Future work

The Codex already supports agents that review code, technical designs, and incident reports. We plan to extend that model throughout the SDLC, allowing agents to surface issues consistently across design, implementation, and operations. The longer-term goal is for agents to identify issues as well as propose fixes with increasing autonomy, while engineers remain responsible for reviewing and approving those changes.

We are also expanding the Codex beyond engineering. Product, security, compliance, and trust and safety teams are beginning to add their own standards, allowing agents to evaluate work against considerations that extend beyond design and implementation alone.

Across a number of engineering workflows, Codex-backed agents have helped us surface issues sooner and apply standards more consistently. We have found AI most useful when it brings the right guidance to engineers at the point of work, and plan to keep extending the approach across Cloudflare.

If you’re interested in building systems like these, our engineering teams are hiring.

sentences.zh: 批准的 RFC 产生非阻塞结果；明确提升后，强制 RFC 会阻止违反 MUST 要求的行为

blocks.html_en: A naive process could stop here and feed the entire Codex to a large language model (LLM) as is. Given the increasing number of RFCs we have already (60+ and counting), however, the corpus volume would put a lot of stress on the context window and impact LLM results negatively. To help guide models to the most relevant RFCs, we invoke a purpose-built agent to automatically extract and compact the SHOULD and MUST statements into a dedicated JSON structure and enrich it with metadata that supports lazy discovery and progressive disclosure. The following abridged excerpt shows the result for our control plane services RFC:

sentences.en: A naive process could stop here and feed the entire Codex to a large language model (LLM) as is.
sentences.zh: 一个幼稚的过程可以在这里停止，并将整个 Codex 按原样输入大型语言模型 (LLM)。

sentences.en: Given the increasing number of RFCs we have already (60+ and counting), however, the corpus volume would put a lot of stress on the context window and impact LLM results negatively.
sentences.zh: 然而，考虑到我们已经拥有的 RFC 数量不断增加（60 多个并且还在增加），语料库数量会给上下文窗口带来很大的压力，并对 LLM 结果产生负面影响。

sentences.en: To help guide models to the most relevant RFCs, we invoke a purpose-built agent to automatically extract and compact the SHOULD and MUST statements into a dedicated JSON structure and enrich it with metadata that supports lazy discovery and progressive disclosure.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助引导模型找到最相关的 RFC，我们调用专门构建的代理来自动提取 SHOULD 和 MUST 语句并将其压缩到专用的 JSON 结构中，并使用支持惰性发现和渐进式披露的元数据来丰富它。

sentences.en: The following abridged excerpt shows the result for our control plane services RFC:
sentences.zh: 以下节选内容显示了我们的控制平面服务 RFC 的结果：

blocks.html_en: Each statement receives a stable slug identifier that remains unchanged during the extraction process even when its RFC is updated. The identifier lets us track the same statement across different systems over time, which is essential for monitoring, analysis, and exception handling.

sentences.en: Each statement receives a stable slug identifier that remains unchanged during the extraction process even when its RFC is updated.
sentences.zh: 每个语句都会收到一个稳定的 slug 标识符，即使其 RFC 更新，该标识符在提取过程中也保持不变。

sentences.en: The identifier lets us track the same statement across different systems over time, which is essential for monitoring, analysis, and exception handling.
sentences.zh: 标识符让我们能够随着时间的推移跟踪不同系统中的相同语句，这对于监视、分析和异常处理至关重要。

blocks.html_en: Initially, we extracted the statements into another, more concise Markdown file rather than JSON. Over time, we moved to a richer structured format so that agents could filter the content they needed more accurately. We plan to include additional metadata for even tighter scoping, such as indicators for the software development life cycle (SDLC) stage a statement applies to (e.g., design, implementation, runtime).

sentences.en: Initially, we extracted the statements into another, more concise Markdown file rather than JSON.
sentences.zh: 最初，我们将语句提取到另一个更简洁的 Markdown 文件中，而不是 JSON。

sentences.en: Over time, we moved to a richer structured format so that agents could filter the content they needed more accurately.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，我们转向了更丰富的结构化格式，以便代理可以更准确地过滤他们需要的内容。

sentences.en: We plan to include additional metadata for even tighter scoping, such as indicators for the software development life cycle (SDLC) stage a statement applies to (e.g., design, implementation, runtime).
sentences.zh: 我们计划包含其他元数据以实现更严格的范围界定，例如声明适用的软件开发生命周期 (SDLC) 阶段的指标（例如设计、实现、运行时）。

sentences.zh: 法典消费者

blocks.html_en: Several systems already use the Codex in day-to-day engineering work. Three agents show how the Codex works in practice: our AI code reviewer, spec reviewer, and incident report reviewer.

sentences.en: Several systems already use the Codex in day-to-day engineering work.
sentences.zh: 一些系统已经在日常工程工作中使用 Codex。

sentences.en: Three agents show how the Codex works in practice: our AI code reviewer, spec reviewer, and incident report reviewer.
sentences.zh: 三位代理展示了 Codex 在实践中的运作方式：我们的 AI 代码审查员、规范审查员和事件报告审查员。

blocks.html_en: AI code reviewer

sentences.en: AI code reviewer
sentences.zh: AI代码审查员

blocks.html_en: Our AI code reviewer agent, covered in a separate blog post, evaluates merge requests across several dimensions, including Codex compliance.

sentences.en: Our AI code reviewer agent, covered in a separate blog post, evaluates merge requests across several dimensions, including Codex compliance.
sentences.zh: 我们的 AI 代码审查代理（在单独的博客文章中介绍）可以跨多个维度评估合并请求，包括 Codex 合规性。

blocks.html_en: For each review, the agent retrieves the RFCs and parses the Codex statements. It loads full RFC bodies only when the model or coordinator needs additional context. In most cases, the statements provide enough information to explain a reported violation.

sentences.en: For each review, the agent retrieves the RFCs and parses the Codex statements.
sentences.zh: 对于每次审查，代理都会检索 RFC 并解析 Codex 声明。

sentences.en: It loads full RFC bodies only when the model or coordinator needs additional context.
sentences.zh: 仅当模型或协调器需要额外的上下文时，它才会加载完整的 RFC 主体。

sentences.en: In most cases, the statements provide enough information to explain a reported violation.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，这些声明提供了足够的信息来解释所报告的违规行为。

blocks.html_en: The distinction between SHOULD and MUST, together with an RFC’s status, determines how the reviewer responds. Findings from approved RFCs are non-blocking recommendations. Once an RFC is enforced, an unsatisfied MUST requirement causes the reviewer to withhold approval or block a merge request, depending on the severity.

sentences.en: The distinction between SHOULD and MUST, together with an RFC’s status, determines how the reviewer responds.
sentences.zh: “应该”和“必须”之间的区别以及 RFC 的状态决定了审阅者的响应方式。

sentences.en: Findings from approved RFCs are non-blocking recommendations.
sentences.zh: 已批准 RFC 的发现是非阻塞建议。

sentences.en: Once an RFC is enforced, an unsatisfied MUST requirement causes the reviewer to withhold approval or block a merge request, depending on the severity.
sentences.zh: 一旦 RFC 被强制执行，不满足的 MUST 要求会导致审阅者拒绝批准或阻止合并请求，具体取决于严重性。

blocks.html_en: Since the Codex’s inception earlier this year, the AI code reviewer has flagged close to 230,000 violations. Among these, almost 16,000 caused approval to be withheld (i.e., they referred to MUST statements on enforced RFCs).

sentences.en: Since the Codex’s inception earlier this year, the AI code reviewer has flagged close to 230,000 violations.
sentences.zh: 自今年早些时候 Codex 成立以来，人工智能代码审查员已标记出近 230,000 起违规行为。

sentences.en: Among these, almost 16,000 caused approval to be withheld (i.e., they referred to MUST statements on enforced RFCs).
sentences.zh: 其中，近 16,000 个导致批准被拒绝（即，它们引用了有关强制 RFC 的 MUST 声明）。

blocks.html_en: Code review alternatives

sentences.en: Code review alternatives
sentences.zh: 代码审查替代方案

blocks.html_en: A single AI code reviewer run usually takes a couple of minutes to complete due to the coordinator framework and sub-agent execution. Although the wait is very often worth the money (or tokens), engineers were calling out the delay and extra round trip involved in remediating the findings. We looked into how we could improve the experience and came up with two additional options:

sentences.en: A single AI code reviewer run usually takes a couple of minutes to complete due to the coordinator framework and sub-agent execution.
sentences.zh: 由于协调器框架和子代理执行，单个 AI 代码审查器运行通常需要几分钟才能完成。

sentences.en: Although the wait is very often worth the money (or tokens), engineers were calling out the delay and extra round trip involved in remediating the findings.
sentences.zh: 尽管等待通常是值得的（或代币），但工程师们指出修复结果所涉及的延迟和额外的往返行程。

sentences.en: We looked into how we could improve the experience and came up with two additional options:
sentences.zh: 我们研究了如何改善体验并提出了两个额外的选择：

blocks.html_en: • For language-specific Codex requirements that can be verified mechanically, we provide custom linter configuration packages. These are aligned with our Codex specification and make it possible to surface problems in milliseconds. TypeScript was the first language to receive Codex linter support while also standardizing on oxlint (maintained by the VoidZero team who joined Cloudflare recently) for performant linter execution. A linter for Rust projects is currently under development, and Go will eventually follow to complete coverage of Cloudflare’s most commonly used languages.

sentences.en: For language-specific Codex requirements that can be verified mechanically, we provide custom linter configuration packages.
sentences.zh: 对于可以机械验证的特定语言的 Codex 要求，我们提供自定义 linter 配置包。

sentences.en: These are aligned with our Codex specification and make it possible to surface problems in milliseconds.
sentences.zh: 这些与我们的 Codex 规范一致，可以在几毫秒内发现问题。

sentences.en: TypeScript was the first language to receive Codex linter support while also standardizing on oxlint (maintained by the VoidZero team who joined Cloudflare recently) for performant linter execution.
sentences.zh: TypeScript 是第一种获得 Codex linter 支持的语言，同时还对 oxlint（由最近加入 Cloudflare 的 VoidZero 团队维护）进行标准化，以实现高性能 linter 执行。

sentences.en: A linter for Rust projects is currently under development, and Go will eventually follow to complete coverage of Cloudflare’s most commonly used languages.
sentences.zh: Rust 项目的 linter 目前正在开发中，Go 最终将完成对 Cloudflare 最常用语言的覆盖。

blocks.html_en: • To cut out the continuous integration (CI) leg from the review cycle, we made it possible to run the AI code reviewer locally through a command-line interface (CLI). It matches the coordinator functionality from CI and runs the same (OpenCode-based) agents against an automatically determined diff set, with results presented in the terminal.

sentences.en: To cut out the continuous integration (CI) leg from the review cycle, we made it possible to run the AI code reviewer locally through a command-line interface (CLI).
sentences.zh: 为了从审查周期中消除持续集成 (CI) 环节，我们可以通过命令行界面 (CLI) 在本地运行 AI 代码审查器。

sentences.en: It matches the coordinator functionality from CI and runs the same (OpenCode-based) agents against an automatically determined diff set, with results presented in the terminal.
sentences.zh: 它与 CI 的协调器功能相匹配，并针对自动确定的差异集运行相同的（基于 OpenCode 的）代理，结果显示在终端中。

blocks.html_en: We believe the linters would be useful to almost every developer and codebase, while the CLI remains an optional alternative for engineers who prefer it.

sentences.en: We believe the linters would be useful to almost every developer and codebase, while the CLI remains an optional alternative for engineers who prefer it.
sentences.zh: 我们相信 linter 对几乎每个开发人员和代码库都有用，而 CLI 仍然是喜欢它的工程师的可选替代方案。

blocks.html_en: Spec reviewer

sentences.en: Spec reviewer
sentences.zh: 规格审查员

blocks.html_en: Engineers at Cloudflare regularly write design documents and technical specifications (or specs in short) before implementation. A significant subset of the Codex pertains to design, architecture, and other themes relevant to technical reviews. To catch architectural mistakes before implementation begins, we built the spec reviewer, an agent that discovers specs and evaluates them against relevant Codex requirements.

sentences.en: Engineers at Cloudflare regularly write design documents and technical specifications (or specs in short) before implementation.
sentences.zh: Cloudflare 的工程师在实施之前定期编写设计文档和技术规范（或简称规范）。

sentences.en: A significant subset of the Codex pertains to design, architecture, and other themes relevant to technical reviews.
sentences.zh: 法典的一个重要子集涉及设计、架构和与技术审查相关的其他主题。

sentences.en: To catch architectural mistakes before implementation begins, we built the spec reviewer, an agent that discovers specs and evaluates them against relevant Codex requirements.
sentences.zh: 为了在实施开始之前发现架构错误，我们构建了规范审查器，这是一个发现规范并根据相关 Codex 要求对其进行评估的代理。

blocks.html_en: The spec reviewer operates on the Developer Platform: it runs as a Cloudflare Worker, stores its results and state in D1, routes model requests through AI Gateway, and kicks off scanning for new specs via a Cron Trigger. It starts by filtering the Codex by domains and sections relevant to specs (for example, language features and implementation-focused RFCs are disregarded). Several guiding prompts instruct the model on how to run the assessment and frame the results. The findings get rated based on severity (influenced by SHOULD and MUST keywords) and include general quality and architectural advice. On completion of a review run, a note is left on the spec document linking to a custom dashboard where review details can be inspected.

sentences.en: The spec reviewer operates on the Developer Platform: it runs as a Cloudflare Worker, stores its results and state in D1, routes model requests through AI Gateway, and kicks off scanning for new specs via a Cron Trigger.
sentences.zh: 规范审核器在开发者平台上运行：它作为 Cloudflare Worker 运行，将其结果和状态存储在 D1 中，通过 AI Gateway 路由模型请求，并通过 Cron 触发器开始扫描新规范。

sentences.en: It starts by filtering the Codex by domains and sections relevant to specs (for example, language features and implementation-focused RFCs are disregarded).
sentences.zh: 它首先按与规范相关的领域和部分过滤 Codex（例如，语言功能和以实现为中心的 RFC 被忽略）。

sentences.zh: 几个指导提示指导模型如何运行评估并构建结果。

sentences.zh: 完成审核运行后，规范文档上会留下一条注释，链接到自定义仪表板，可以在其中检查审核详细信息。

blocks.html_en: Since the beginning of May 2026, almost 600 unique open specs have been reviewed. Including reruns triggered on demand or by spec changes, we tracked over 3,200 review invocations to this date. The vast majority of findings had a “major” (65%) or “minor” (29%) severity, with “critical” findings being the minority (6%).

sentences.zh: 自 2026 年 5 月开始，已经审核了近 600 个独特的开放规范。

sentences.en: Including reruns triggered on demand or by spec changes, we tracked over 3,200 review invocations to this date.
sentences.zh: 包括按需或规范更改触发的重新运行，迄今为止我们跟踪了 3,200 多个审核调用。

blocks.html_en: The incident report reviewer applies the same approach to incident reports (also known as postmortems). In addition to checking that each report is complete, it evaluates whether the report clearly explains what happened, identifies contributing factors, documents the resolution, and proposes meaningful follow-up actions. These expectations are defined in a dedicated Codex RFC.

For high-severity incidents, we’ve made the reviewer mandatory as part of our comprehensive central review process, and reports are not considered complete until all findings have been addressed.

content_html_zh:
在过去的四个月里，我们的 AI 代码审查员标记了近 25 万个与 Cloudflare 工程标准的偏差（我们在本文中称之为“违规”），并阻止了 16,000 个合并。 在实施开始之前，我们的规范审查代理已根据相同标准评估了近 600 项技术设计。 这两个系统都取材于 Cloudflare Codex，这是一个为人员和代理构建的工程指导共享源。 这篇文章解释了我们构建 Codex 的原因、它如何支持工程生命周期以及我们下一步计划做什么。

在 Codex（我们在之前关于 AI 工程堆栈的文章中简要介绍过）之前，Cloudflare 的开发人员指南存在于许多地方：正式文档、存储库文件、聊天线程以及各个工程师积累的知识。 工程师常常花费太多时间寻找指导，而不是致力于解决他们想要解决的问题。 即使找到答案后，他们也不能总是判断它是否是最新的、权威的或适用于他们的情况。

随着 Cloudflare 的发展，这种模式变得越来越难以维持。 没有工程师可以阅读每个标准，审阅者也无法可靠地检查每个要求。 当人们在团队之间流动时，机构知识变得更难恢复，并且不一致的指导或执行会导致项目之间的漂移。

我们将这一知识体系重建为 Cloudflare Codex：一组受管理的工程标准，代理可以在工作时检索和应用这些标准。 现在，相同的指南可以为代码审查、技术设计审查、事件报告审查和许多其他用例提供信息，而工程师则将时间和判断集中在结果发现上。

法典组织和工作流程

专门的 Codex 治理模型将 Codex 划分为涵盖我们关心的工程领域的不同领域。 其中包括架构问题（例如，前端和控制平面）、横切问题（安全性和可靠性）、特定语言（TypeScript 和 Rust）以及其他几个领域。 每个域都由一个所有者领导，该所有者对其所监管的文档的内容、一致性和整体质量负责。

法典标准使用征求意见 (RFC) 格式。 要求使用 RFC 2119 定义的 SHOULD 和 MUST 关键字。 我们还期望 Front Matter 标头能够保存域和 RFC 状态等元数据。 任何具有关键兴趣和领域能力的 Cloudflare 员工都可以通过遵循规定结构的合并请求提出 RFC。 然后，该提案会经过越来越广泛的评审者群体的多轮反馈。 一旦域名所有者给予最终批准，RFC 就会成为 Codex 的一部分，并发布到 Astro 支持的内部站点。

批准的 RFC 可以由 Codex 客户端和代理使用，然后可以立即开始标记代码、配置或文档中的 Codex 违规行为。 但是，只有在 RFC 从已批准生命周期状态转变为强制生命周期状态后，它们才会根据 Codex 声明进行阻止。 这一单独的升级步骤使团队有时间吸收新的要求，并适应执行需要额外工作的情况。

一个幼稚的过程可以在这里停止，并将整个 Codex 按原样输入大型语言模型 (LLM)。 然而，考虑到我们已经拥有的 RFC 数量不断增加（60 多个并且还在增加），语料库数量会给上下文窗口带来很大的压力，并对 LLM 结果产生负面影响。 为了帮助引导模型找到最相关的 RFC，我们调用专门构建的代理来自动提取 SHOULD 和 MUST 语句并将其压缩到专用的 JSON 结构中，并使用支持惰性发现和渐进式披露的元数据来丰富它。 以下节选内容显示了我们的控制平面服务 RFC 的结果：

{
  "rfc": 14,
  "title": "Control Plane Services",
  "status": "approved",
  "domain": "control-plane",
  "statements": [
    {
      "slug": "use-quicksilver-for-edge-configuration-propagation",
      "section": ["Proposal", "Infrastructure"],
      "level": "SHOULD",
      "text": "If you need to propagate system or customer configuration to the edge, use Quicksilver via the outbox pattern",
      "href": "/rfcs/014-control-plane-services/#infrastructure"
    },
    {
      "slug": "api-schemas-must-be-documented-in-openapi-spec",
      "section": ["Proposal", "API Gateway"],
      "level": "MUST",
      "text": "API request and response schemas MUST be documented using an OpenAPI spec",
      "href": "/rfcs/014-control-plane-services/#api-gateway"
    }
  ]
}

每个语句都会收到一个稳定的 slug 标识符，即使其 RFC 更新，该标识符在提取过程中也保持不变。 标识符让我们能够随着时间的推移跟踪不同系统中的相同语句，这对于监视、分析和异常处理至关重要。

最初，我们将语句提取到另一个更简洁的 Markdown 文件中，而不是 JSON。 随着时间的推移，我们转向了更丰富的结构化格式，以便代理可以更准确地过滤他们需要的内容。 我们计划包含其他元数据以实现更严格的范围界定，例如声明适用的软件开发生命周期 (SDLC) 阶段的指标（例如设计、实现、运行时）。

法典消费者

一些系统已经在日常工程工作中使用 Codex。 三位代理展示了 Codex 在实践中的运作方式：我们的 AI 代码审查员、规范审查员和事件报告审查员。

AI代码审查员

我们的 AI 代码审查代理（在单独的博客文章中介绍）可以跨多个维度评估合并请求，包括 Codex 合规性。

对于每次审查，代理都会检索 RFC 并解析 Codex 声明。 仅当模型或协调器需要额外的上下文时，它才会加载完整的 RFC 主体。 在大多数情况下，这些声明提供了足够的信息来解释所报告的违规行为。

“应该”和“必须”之间的区别以及 RFC 的状态决定了审阅者的响应方式。 已批准 RFC 的发现是非阻塞建议。 一旦 RFC 被强制执行，不满足的 MUST 要求会导致审阅者拒绝批准或阻止合并请求，具体取决于严重性。

自今年早些时候 Codex 成立以来，人工智能代码审查员已标记出近 230,000 起违规行为。 其中，近 16,000 个导致批准被拒绝（即，它们引用了有关强制 RFC 的 MUST 声明）。

代码审查替代方案

由于协调器框架和子代理执行，单个 AI 代码审查器运行通常需要几分钟才能完成。 尽管等待通常是值得的（或代币），但工程师们指出修复结果所涉及的延迟和额外的往返行程。 我们研究了如何改善体验并提出了两个额外的选择：

  1. 对于可以机械验证的特定语言的 Codex 要求，我们提供自定义 linter 配置包。 这些与我们的 Codex 规范一致，可以在几毫秒内发现问题。 TypeScript 是第一种获得 Codex linter 支持的语言，同时还对 oxlint（由最近加入 Cloudflare 的 VoidZero 团队维护）进行标准化，以实现高性能 linter 执行。 Rust 项目的 linter 目前正在开发中，Go 最终将完成对 Cloudflare 最常用语言的覆盖。
  2. 为了从审查周期中消除持续集成 (CI) 环节，我们可以通过命令行界面 (CLI) 在本地运行 AI 代码审查器。 它与 CI 的协调器功能相匹配，并针对自动确定的差异集运行相同的（基于 OpenCode 的）代理，结果显示在终端中。

我们相信 linter 对几乎每个开发人员和代码库都有用，而 CLI 仍然是喜欢它的工程师的可选替代方案。

规格审查员

Cloudflare 的工程师在实施之前定期编写设计文档和技术规范（或简称规范）。 法典的一个重要子集涉及设计、架构和与技术审查相关的其他主题。 为了在实施开始之前发现架构错误，我们构建了规范审查器，这是一个发现规范并根据相关 Codex 要求对其进行评估的代理。

规范审核器在开发者平台上运行：它作为 Cloudflare Worker 运行，将其结果和状态存储在 D1 中，通过 AI Gateway 路由模型请求，并通过 Cron 触发器开始扫描新规范。 它首先按与规范相关的领域和部分过滤 Codex（例如，语言功能和以实现为中心的 RFC 被忽略）。 几个指导提示指导模型如何运行评估并构建结果。 结果根据严重性（受“应该”和“必须”关键字的影响）进行评级，并包括一般质量和架构建议。 完成审核运行后，规范文档上会留下一条注释，链接到自定义仪表板，可以在其中检查审核详细信息。

自 2026 年 5 月开始，已经审核了近 600 个独特的开放规范。 包括按需或规范更改触发的重新运行，迄今为止我们跟踪了 3,200 多个审核调用。 绝大多数调查结果的严重程度为“严重”（65%）或“轻微”（29%），“严重”调查结果为少数（6%）。

事故报告审核员

事件报告审阅者对事件报告采用相同的方法（也称为事后分析）。 除了检查每份报告是否完整之外，它还评估报告是否清楚地解释了发生的情况、确定影响因素、记录解决方案并提出有意义的后续行动。 这些期望在专门的 Codex RFC 中定义。

事件报告审阅者使用与规范审阅者相同的开发者平台构建块。 这种共享架构正在成为我们 Codex 代理的常见模式。

自 2026 年 5 月以来，审核人员评估了 200 多份事件报告，并发现了缺失后续行动项目、时间表不完整和遗漏检测信号等缺陷。 在这些报告中，93% 的事件属于低影响、仅限内部或先发制人的事件。 对于高严重性事件，我们已强制要求审核员作为我们全面中央审核流程的一部分，并且在所有调查结果得到解决之前，报告不会被视为完整。

未来的工作

Codex 已经支持审查代码、技术设计和事件报告的代理。 我们计划在整个 SDLC 中扩展该模型，使代理能够在设计、实施和运营中一致地提出问题。 长期目标是让代理能够识别问题并提出修复方案，同时增加自主权，而工程师仍然负责审查和批准这些更改。

我们还将 Codex 扩展到工程之外。 产品、安全、合规以及信任和安全团队开始添加自己的标准，使代理能够根据超出设计和实施范围的考虑因素来评估工作。

在许多工程工作流程中，Codex 支持的代理帮助我们更快地发现问题并更一致地应用标准。 我们发现，当人工智能在工作时为工程师提供正确的指导时，它最有用，并计划在 Cloudflare 中继续扩展该方法。
